title: Step P8: independent worked example of Building B's placement on lot 70 and its area allocation, written into the R6B reference cases as one case placement-building-b (two sealed readings; a value only where both agree on the same basis; placement on the printed-tax-map basis A1, the city-map outline a conflict check only; the area illustration on the one stated 60% share; the plate is zoning floor area per storey, no physical-plate conversion worked; NO rule file, engine, result, capture, register entry or human verdict)
objective: A new R6B reference case placement-building-b built from the two step-P8 sealed readings (returns kept unchanged as provenance -17 and -18): the footprint, placement and area allocation of the three-storey Building B (20,150 sq ft zoning floor area, 10-ft floor-to-floor) on lot 70 of block 7334 under Z1 (lot 70 alone). A value or figure is recorded only where both readings give it on the same words and the same basis; every disagreement or unresolved basis stays NOT SETTLED with both readings named and the kind of gap stated. Placement is on the printed-tax-map basis (A1); the city-map (GIS) outline is used only as a conflict check (e.g. the south offset 33.34 tax map / 33.32 map outline, and the ~3.12 ft depth-basis conflict stay not known). The plate is recorded as zoning floor area per storey (20,150 / 3 = 6,716.67) with the footprint figure (about 100.76 x 66.66 = 6,716.66) reconciled within the readers' tolerance, every such figure labelled 'plate = zoning floor area per storey; no gross-up, exclusions or wall-thickness conversion worked'; the physical floor plate (gross-up, exclusions, wall thickness) is listed as not checked. The area allocation applies the one stated 60% apartment-area share to the proposed building's residential floor area (the same measure as the estimate): apartment area and other area per storey and in total, summing to the total. Every quantity names exactly one of the nine measurement bases; no figure mixes bases; no value anywhere comes from a program run. The case is wired into the reference-case support (CASE_IDS, REQUIRED_BASE_IDS, the checker, provenance digests) and the two consumer pins a new case moves are updated.
business_reason: D-094 R043/R076/R082: the first complete scenario needs a footprint placed on the site, worked from source facts and law before the report/drawing and the engine consume it (M5-T172 later takes its expected values from this case, never from program output); R091/R092: the area illustration uses one stated share on a measure compatible with the estimate.

acceptance_scenarios.then: both are present unchanged below a short header, each says it was made from the sealed folder and ends with END-OF-REPORT, and their digests are pinned in r6b_reference_cases_step_p8; a changed reading is caught
each names both readings (-17 and -18) and quotes captured words found in the cited capture by its file name

acceptance_scenarios.given: a point the two readings do not jointly settle (the south offset 33.34 tax map / 33.32 map outline, the ~3.12 ft depth-basis conflict, or any coverage bound the captured text does not fix)
acceptance_scenarios.then: it stays NOT SETTLED with both readings named and the kind of gap stated; a value where they differ is refused

acceptance_scenarios.given: the plate on the stated measure
acceptance_scenarios.then: the plate is recorded as zoning floor area per storey (20,150 / 3 = 6,716.67) and the footprint figure (about 100.76 x 66.66 = 6,716.66) separately, each pinned to its exact recompute and reconciled within the readers' +/- 0.5 sq ft; each carries 'plate = zoning floor area per storey; no gross-up, exclusions or wall-thickness conversion worked'; the physical floor plate is listed as not checked; every quantity carries exactly one of the nine bases

acceptance_scenarios.given: the area allocation at the one stated 60% apartment-area share
acceptance_scenarios.then: apartment area and other area are recorded per storey and in total on the proposed building's residential floor area (12,090 apartment / 8,060 other of 20,150; 4,030 / 2,686.67 per storey), apartment + other equals the total, and every arithmetic step recomputes exactly

acceptance_scenarios.when: the real-lot placement rows are written
acceptance_scenarios.then: the city-map outline is used only as a conflict check; no row records a placement or coverage conclusion that omits its basis or the Z1 zoning-lot condition

placement-building-b is in CASE_IDS (lib and the pinned tuple at test_r6b_reference_cases.py), REQUIRED_BASE_IDS has its entry, README lists it, the rendered page is byte-identical, the step-p7 PRIOR_ROWS_DIGEST is updated, the other cases' rows stay byte-stable, program_result_errors is empty, and every support .py stays under 600 SLOC

risks: The readings may differ on the placement basis or the offsets; then those rows stay NOT SETTLED and any later report/drawing shows not known.

20,150/3 = 6,716.67 but 100.76 x 66.66 = 6,716.66: the +/- 0.5 is the readers' agreement tolerance, not an engine tolerance - the reference-case engine compares each step exactly, so the plate and the footprint are separate rows/quantities each pinned to its own exact recompute; do not force one figure.
r6b_reference_cases_check.py is at 580 SLOC against the 600-SLOC focus cap; the step-P8 wiring must stay thin (all new guards live in r6b_reference_cases_step_p8.py).
The sealed folder lives on the private build server: the case records its inputs by name and digest, never third-party text in bulk.
path_notes: Engine-free: the support code imports nothing from app. The producer receives the two readings as files and copies them unchanged into provenance -17/-18. Author the case with existing render constructs (facts, citations, arithmetic steps, quantities, not_known); do NOT reuse the step-p6 numbers_block differ-figure, whose 'reading 13 / reading 14' labels are hardcoded in render.py:238-240 and would mislabel step-P8. Keep render.py byte-identical unless a new construct is genuinely needed. Builders never start a server and never touch ports 3000/3001/8000. Does not touch the benchmark set (G-5) or NB-01 code paths (G-6); must be the sole reference-case task in flight while open.
